questions.q: If set A has 3 elements and set B has 2 elements, how many elements does A × B have?
If the ordered pairs (x + 1, y − 2) and (3, 1) are equal, find x + y.
questions.e: x + 1 = 3 gives x = 2 and y − 2 = 1 gives y = 3, so x + y = 5.

questions.q: If f(x) = x² − 3x + 2, find f(4).
If n(A) = 2 and n(B) = 3, how many relations are there from A to B?
questions.e: A × B has 2 × 3 = 6 elements; every subset is a relation, so there are 2⁶ = 64 relations.

questions.q: If f(x) = 2x + 3 and g(x) = x² are real functions, find (fg)(2).
If A = {1, 2}, how many elements does A × A × A have?
The domain of the real function f(x) = (x² + 1)/(x² − 5x + 6) is R − {a, b}. Find a + b.
questions.e: x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0 at x = 2 and x = 3, so the domain is R − {2, 3} and a + b = 5.

questions.q: R = {(x, y) : y = x + 5, x is a natural number less than 4}. Find the sum of all elements in the range of R.
questions.e: x = 1, 2, 3 gives y = 6, 7, 8, so the range is {6, 7, 8} and its sum is 21.

questions.q: Let A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 6} and R = {(a, b) : a, b ∈ A, b is exactly divisible by a}. How many ordered pairs are there in R?
If f(x) = x³ − 1/x³ (x ≠ 0), find the value of f(x) + f(1/x).
questions.e: f(1/x) = 1/x³ − x³, so f(x) + f(1/x) = x³ − 1/x³ + 1/x³ − x³ = 0.

questions.q: A relation R in a set A is called a ______ relation if R = A × A.
questions.e: If every element of A is related to every element of A, i.e. R = A × A, the relation is called the universal relation.

questions.q: A function f : X → Y is said to be ______ if every element of Y is the image of some element of X under f.
questions.e: f is onto (surjective) if for every y ∈ Y there exists x ∈ X with f(x) = y, i.e. range = codomain.

questions.q: How many ordered pairs are there in the identity relation on a set having 4 elements?
questions.e: The identity relation contains only the pairs (a, a), one for each element, so it has 4 pairs.

questions.q: How many equivalence relations on the set {1, 2, 3} contain the ordered pair (1, 2)?
questions.e: 1 and 2 must be in the same class: either {1, 2}, {3} or {1, 2, 3}. So there are 2 such equivalence relations.

questions.q: How many one-one functions are there from the set {1, 2, 3} to itself?
questions.e: A one-one function from a 3-element set to itself is a permutation, so there are 3! = 6.

questions.q: On A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}, R = {(a, b) : |a − b| is even} is an equivalence relation. How many elements of A are related to 1 (including 1 itself)?
questions.e: |a − 1| is even for a = 1, 3, 5, so the equivalence class of 1 is {1, 3, 5}, which has 3 elements.

questions.q: Let R = {(1, 2), (2, 3)} be a relation on {1, 2, 3}. What is the minimum number of ordered pairs that must be added to R to make it both reflexive and transitive?
questions.e: Reflexivity needs (1,1), (2,2), (3,3); transitivity of (1,2) and (2,3) needs (1,3). The resulting set is reflexive and transitive, so 4 pairs are needed.

questions.q: How many onto functions are there from the set {1, 2, 3} to the set {a, b}?
questions.e: Total functions = 2³ = 8; the 2 constant functions are not onto, so onto functions = 8 − 2 = 6.

questions.q: How many different equivalence relations can be defined on a set with 3 elements?
questions.e: Equivalence relations correspond to partitions: {a}{b}{c}, {ab}{c}, {ac}{b}, {bc}{a}, {abc} — 5 in total.

questions.q: How many reflexive relations can be defined on a set with 3 elements?
questions.e: A × A has 9 pairs; the 3 diagonal pairs must be included and each of the other 6 may or may not be, giving 2⁶ = 64.

questions.q: What is the order of the differential equation d²y/dx² + (dy/dx)³ + y = 0?
questions.e: The highest order derivative present is d²y/dx², so the order is 2.

questions.q: What is the degree of the differential equation (d²y/dx²)³ + (dy/dx)⁴ + y = 0?
questions.e: The equation is a polynomial in derivatives; the highest order derivative d²y/dx² occurs with power 3, so the degree is 3.

questions.q: How many arbitrary constants are there in the general solution of a differential equation of order 3?
questions.e: The general solution of an nth order differential equation contains n arbitrary constants, so here 3.

questions.q: Find the sum of the order and the degree of the differential equation (d³y/dx³)² + (d²y/dx²)³ + dy/dx + y = 0.
questions.e: Highest order derivative is d³y/dx³ (order 3), and its power is 2 (degree 2); 3 + 2 = 5.

questions.q: Solve dy/dx = 2x with y(0) = 1. What is the value of y when x = 3?
questions.e: y = x² + C; y(0) = 1 gives C = 1, so y = x² + 1 and y(3) = 10.

questions.q: Solve dy/dx = y with y(0) = 2. What is the value of y when x = ln 3?
questions.e: dy/y = dx gives y = Ce^x; y(0) = 2 gives C = 2, so y = 2e^(ln 3) = 6.

questions.q: Solve the linear differential equation dy/dx + y/x = 3x (x > 0) with y(1) = 2. What is the value of y when x = 2?
questions.e: IF = x, so d(xy)/dx = 3x², giving xy = x³ + C; y(1) = 2 gives C = 1. At x = 2: 2y = 9, so y = 4.5.

questions.q: Solve the homogeneous differential equation x dy/dx = x + y (x > 0) with y(1) = 2. What is the value of y/x when x = e?
questions.e: dy/dx − y/x = 1 has IF 1/x, so d(y/x)/dx = 1/x and y/x = ln x + C; y(1) = 2 gives C = 2. At x = e, y/x = 1 + 2 = 3.

questions.q: Solve dy/dx + 2y = 4 with y(0) = 0. What is the value of y when x = ln 2?
Solve (1 + x²) dy/dx = 2xy with y(0) = 1. What is the value of y when x = 3?
questions.e: dy/y = 2x dx/(1 + x²) gives ln y = ln(1 + x²) + C; y(0) = 1 gives C = 0, so y = 1 + x² and y(3) = 10.

questions.q: If A = {1, 2, 3, 4} and B = {3, 4, 5}, how many elements does A ∪ B have?
questions.e: A ∪ B = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}, which has 5 elements.

questions.q: How many subsets does a set with 4 elements have?
questions.e: A set with n elements has 2ⁿ subsets: 2⁴ = 16.

questions.q: If A = {2, 4, 6, 8} and B = {6, 8, 10}, how many elements does A ∩ B have?
How many proper subsets does the set {a, b, c} have?
questions.e: It has 2³ = 8 subsets; all except the set itself are proper: 7.

questions.q: U = {1, 2, 3, …, 10} and A = {1, 3, 5, 7, 9}. How many elements does A′, the complement of A, have?
questions.e: A′ = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10}, which has 5 elements.

questions.q: In a class of 40 students, 25 like cricket, 20 like football and 10 like both. How many like neither?
questions.e: n(C ∪ F) = 25 + 20 − 10 = 35, so 40 − 35 = 5 like neither.

questions.q: If n(A) = 3, how many elements does P(A) × P(A) have?
questions.e: P(A) has 2³ = 8 elements, so P(A) × P(A) has 8 × 8 = 64.

questions.q: In a survey of 100 people, 60 read newspaper H, 50 read newspaper T and 30 read both. How many read exactly one of the two?
questions.e: Only H: 60 − 30 = 30; only T: 50 − 30 = 20; exactly one: 30 + 20 = 50.

questions.q: In a group of 65 people, everyone likes cricket or tennis or both. 40 like cricket and 10 like both. How many like tennis?
Convert π/4 radians into degrees.
questions.e: π radians = 180°, so π/4 = 45°.

questions.q: What is the value of sin 30°?
Find the value of cos 60° + sin 90°.
questions.e: cos 60° = 0.5 and sin 90° = 1, so the sum is 1.5.

questions.q: The period of sin x is kπ. What is k?
questions.e: sin(x + 2π) = sin x for every x, and no smaller positive number works, so the period is 2π.

questions.q: If sin x = 3/5 and x is in the first quadrant, find cos x.
questions.e: cos x = √(1 − 9/25) = 4/5 = 0.8, positive in the first quadrant.

questions.q: Find the value of tan 45° + cot 45°.
Find the value of sin² 30° + cos² 30° + tan² 45°.
questions.e: sin² θ + cos² θ = 1 and tan² 45° = 1, so the total is 2.

questions.q: Find the value of cos 15° × cos 75°.
questions.e: cos 75° = sin 15°, so the product is sin 15° cos 15° = ½ sin 30° = 0.25.

questions.q: If tan x = 3/4 and x lies in the third quadrant, find sin x + cos x.
questions.e: In the third quadrant sine and cosine are negative: sin x = −3/5 and cos x = −4/5, so the sum is −7/5 = −1.4.

questions.q: If tan x = 2, find cos 2x. (cos 2x = (1 − tan² x)/(1 + tan² x))
What is the value of i²?
questions.e: By definition i = √−1, so i² = −1.

questions.q: What is the real part of 3 − 4i?
questions.e: For z = a + ib, the real part is a = 3; the imaginary part is −4.

questions.q: Find the modulus of 3 + 4i.
Find the value of i¹⁰.
questions.e: i⁴ = 1, so i¹⁰ = (i⁴)² × i² = −1.

questions.q: If z = 2 + 3i, find z × z̄ (z times its conjugate).
Find the imaginary part of (1 + i)².
Find the modulus of (1 + i)/(1 − i).
questions.e: |1 + i| = |1 − i| = √2, so the modulus of the quotient is 1. (In fact (1 + i)/(1 − i) = i.)

questions.q: Find the sum 1 + i + i² + i³ + … + i²⁰.
questions.e: Every four consecutive powers add to 0. The 21 terms are five groups of four (sum 0) plus i²⁰ = 1.

questions.q: Find the real part of (3 + 2i)/(1 − i).
questions.e: Multiply top and bottom by 1 + i: (3 + 2i)(1 + i)/2 = (3 + 5i + 2i²)/2 = (1 + 5i)/2. The real part is 0.5.

questions.q: If z1 = 2 − i and z2 = 1 + i, find |z1 + z2|².
What is the largest integer x that satisfies 3x < 12?
questions.e: 3x < 12 gives x < 4, so the largest integer is 3.

questions.q: What is the smallest integer x that satisfies x + 5 > 8?
questions.e: x > 3, so the smallest integer is 4.

questions.q: If x < 5, which of these is true?
questions.e: Multiplying both sides of an inequality by a negative number reverses the sign.

questions.q: How many natural numbers satisfy 2x − 3 < 7?
questions.e: 2x < 10 gives x < 5, so x = 1, 2, 3 or 4.

questions.q: Find the smallest integer x that satisfies 5x − 3 ≥ 3x + 1.
Find the least value of x that satisfies (x − 1)/3 ≥ 2.
How many integers satisfy −5 ≤ 2x + 1 < 7?
Ravi scored 70 and 75 in two tests. What is the least he must score in the third test for an average of at least 60?
How many pairs of consecutive odd positive integers, both smaller than 10, have a sum greater than 11?
questions.e: Let them be x and x + 2: x + 2 < 10 and 2x + 2 > 11 give 4.5 < x < 8, so x = 5 or 7: the pairs (5, 7) and (7, 9).

questions.q: 640 litres of an 8% boric acid solution is to be diluted by adding a 2% solution so that the mixture is between 4% and 6%. The volume added must be more than how many litres?
questions.e: For less than 6%: 0.08(640) + 0.02x < 0.06(640 + x) gives x > 320. For more than 4%: x < 1280. So between 320 L and 1280 L must be added.

questions.q: Find 5! (5 factorial).
In how many ways can 3 different books be arranged on a shelf?
Find ⁵C₂.
How many 3-digit numbers can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 if no digit is repeated?
How many words (with or without meaning) can be formed using each letter of EQUATION exactly once?
questions.e: EQUATION has 8 different letters, so there are 8! = 40320 arrangements.

questions.q: In how many ways can a committee of 3 be chosen from 7 people?
How many arrangements of the letters of ALLAHABAD are possible?
questions.e: 9 letters with A four times and L twice: 9!/(4! 2!) = 362880/48 = 7560.

questions.q: If ⁿC₈ = ⁿC₂, find n.
questions.e: ⁿCₐ = ⁿC_b with a ≠ b means a + b = n, so n = 8 + 2 = 10.

questions.q: A committee of 3 men and 2 women is to be chosen from 5 men and 4 women. In how many ways can it be done?
How many 4-digit even numbers can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 if no digit is repeated?
questions.e: The last digit must be 2 or 4 (2 ways); the other three places are filled from the remaining 4 digits in 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 ways: 2 × 24 = 48.

questions.q: How many terms are there in the expansion of (a + b)⁷?
questions.e: (a + b)ⁿ has n + 1 terms.

questions.q: What is the coefficient of x² in (1 + x)⁴?
questions.e: The coefficient is ⁴C₂ = 6.

questions.q: What is the sum of the binomial coefficients in the expansion of (1 + x)⁵?
What is the coefficient of the middle term of (1 + x)⁶?
questions.e: There are 7 terms; the middle one is the 4th, with coefficient ⁶C₃ = 20.

questions.q: Find the coefficient of x³ in (x + 2)⁵.
questions.e: The term is ⁵C₂ x³ 2² = 10 × 4 x³ = 40x³.

questions.q: Find the constant term in the expansion of (x + 1/x)⁴.
questions.e: The general term is ⁴C_r x^(4 − 2r); it is constant when r = 2: ⁴C₂ = 6.

questions.q: Use the binomial theorem to find (1.1)⁴ exactly.
Find the coefficient of x⁵ in (x + 3)⁸.
questions.e: The term is ⁸C₃ x⁵ 3³ = 56 × 27 x⁵ = 1512x⁵.

questions.q: In the expansion of (1 + x)ⁿ, the coefficients of the 2nd and 3rd terms are equal. Find n.
questions.e: ⁿC₁ = ⁿC₂ gives n = n(n − 1)/2, so n − 1 = 2 and n = 3.

questions.q: Find the term independent of x in the expansion of (x² + 1/x)⁶.
questions.e: The general term is ⁶C_r x^(2(6 − r)) x^(−r) = ⁶C_r x^(12 − 3r). It is constant when r = 4: ⁶C₄ = 15.

questions.q: Find the 10th term of the AP 2, 5, 8, …
Find the common ratio of the GP 3, 6, 12, 24, …
Find the sum of the first 10 natural numbers.
Find the sum of the first 20 terms of the AP 1, 3, 5, …
questions.e: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n² = 400.

questions.q: Find the 6th term of the GP 2, 6, 18, …
Find the geometric mean of 4 and 16.
Find the sum to infinity of the GP 1, 1/2, 1/4, …
Find 1² + 2² + 3² + … + 10².
The sum of the first n terms of an AP is 3n² + 2n. Find its 5th term.
Two numbers are inserted between 3 and 81 so that the four numbers form a GP. What is the larger number inserted?
questions.e: 3r³ = 81 gives r = 3, so the GP is 3, 9, 27, 81.

questions.q: Find the slope of the line through (1, 2) and (3, 8).
What is the slope of a line parallel to the x-axis?
questions.e: A horizontal line makes an angle of 0° with the x-axis, and tan 0° = 0.

questions.q: Find the distance between the points (0, 0) and (6, 8).
Find the y-intercept of the line 2x + 3y = 12.
questions.e: Put x = 0: 3y = 12, so y = 4.

questions.q: Find the slope of the line 3x − 4y + 5 = 0.
questions.e: y = (3/4)x + 5/4, so the slope is 3/4 = 0.75.

questions.q: A line has slope √3. What angle does it make with the positive x-axis?
questions.e: tan θ = √3 gives θ = 60°.

questions.q: Find the distance of the point (3, −5) from the line 3x − 4y − 26 = 0.
Find the distance between the parallel lines 3x − 4y + 7 = 0 and 3x − 4y + 5 = 0.
The line through (2, 3) and (4, k) is perpendicular to a line of slope −1/2. Find k.
questions.e: Perpendicular slopes multiply to −1, so the slope must be 2: (k − 3)/2 = 2 gives k = 7.

questions.q: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 6).
questions.e: It is a right triangle with legs 4 and 6: ½ × 4 × 6 = 12.

questions.q: Find the radius of the circle x² + y² = 49.
questions.e: x² + y² = r² with r² = 49, so r = 7.

questions.q: What is the eccentricity of a circle?
questions.e: A circle is an ellipse with both foci at the centre: e = 0.

questions.q: Find the length of the latus rectum of the parabola y² = 12x.
questions.e: For y² = 4ax the latus rectum is 4a; here 4a = 12.

questions.q: Find the radius of the circle x² + y² − 4x − 6y − 12 = 0.
questions.e: Completing squares: (x − 2)² + (y − 3)² = 4 + 9 + 12 = 25, so r = 5.

questions.q: The focus of the parabola y² = 8x is (a, 0). Find a.
questions.e: y² = 4ax with 4a = 8, so a = 2 and the focus is (2, 0).

questions.q: Find the length of the major axis of the ellipse x²/25 + y²/9 = 1.
questions.e: a² = 25, so a = 5 and the major axis is 2a = 10.

questions.q: Find the eccentricity of the ellipse x²/25 + y²/16 = 1.
questions.e: c² = a² − b² = 9, so c = 3 and e = c/a = 3/5 = 0.6.

questions.q: Find the eccentricity of the hyperbola x²/9 − y²/16 = 1. Give two decimal places.
questions.e: c² = a² + b² = 25, so c = 5 and e = 5/3 ≈ 1.67.

questions.q: Find the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse x²/36 + y²/16 = 1. (Latus rectum = 2b²/a.) Give two decimal places.
A hyperbola has foci (±5, 0) and vertices (±3, 0), so its equation is x²/9 − y²/b² = 1. Find b².
questions.e: c² = a² + b²: 25 = 9 + b², so b² = 16.

questions.q: Find the limit of x² + 1 as x → 2.
questions.e: Polynomials are continuous, so substitute: 4 + 1 = 5.

questions.q: Find the derivative of x³ at x = 2.
questions.e: d/dx (x³) = 3x² = 12 at x = 2.

questions.q: What is the derivative of a constant?
questions.e: A constant does not change, so its rate of change is 0.

questions.q: Find the limit of (x² − 9)/(x − 3) as x → 3.
questions.e: (x² − 9)/(x − 3) = x + 3 for x ≠ 3, which tends to 6.

questions.q: Find the limit of sin(4x)/x as x → 0.
questions.e: sin(4x)/x = 4 × sin(4x)/(4x), which tends to 4 × 1 = 4.

questions.q: Find the derivative of 5x² + 3x at x = 1.
Find the limit of (x¹⁰ − 1)/(x − 1) as x → 1.
questions.e: lim (xⁿ − aⁿ)/(x − a) = naⁿ⁻¹, which is 10 × 1⁹ = 10.

questions.q: If f(x) = x sin x, find f′(0).
questions.e: By the product rule f′(x) = sin x + x cos x, so f′(0) = 0.

questions.q: Find the limit of (1 − cos x)/x² as x → 0.
questions.e: 1 − cos x = 2 sin²(x/2), so the expression = ½ [sin(x/2)/(x/2)]², which tends to ½.

questions.q: Find the derivative of (x + 1)/x at x = 1.
questions.e: (x + 1)/x = 1 + 1/x, whose derivative is −1/x² = −1 at x = 1.

questions.q: Find the mean of 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10.
Find the range of the data 7, 3, 9, 15, 4.
questions.e: Range = largest − smallest = 15 − 3 = 12.

questions.q: Find the median of 3, 7, 1, 9, 5.
questions.e: In order: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. The middle value is 5.

questions.q: Find the variance of 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10.
questions.e: Mean = 6; squared deviations 16, 4, 0, 4, 16 add to 40; variance = 40/5 = 8.

questions.q: Find the standard deviation of 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10. Give two decimal places.
questions.e: The variance is 8, so σ = √8 ≈ 2.83.

questions.q: Find the mean deviation about the mean of 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10.
questions.e: Mean = 6; absolute deviations 4, 2, 0, 2, 4 add to 12; 12/5 = 2.4.

questions.q: Five observations have a mean of 4.4 and a variance of 8.24. Three of them are 1, 2 and 6. Find the sum of the other two.
questions.e: The total is 5 × 4.4 = 22, so the other two add to 22 − 9 = 13. (They are 4 and 9.)

questions.q: If every observation is multiplied by 3, the variance becomes how many times larger?
questions.e: Each deviation is multiplied by 3, so each squared deviation, and the variance, by 9.

questions.q: For 10 observations, Σx = 50 and Σx² = 300. Find the variance.
questions.e: Mean = 5; variance = Σx²/n − mean² = 30 − 25 = 5.

questions.q: The mean of 100 observations was found to be 40. Later it was found that one value had been taken as 50 instead of 40. Find the correct mean.
questions.e: Correct total = 4000 − 50 + 40 = 3990, so the mean is 39.9.

questions.q: A fair die is thrown. What is the probability of getting an even number?
questions.e: Three of the six outcomes (2, 4, 6) are even: 3/6 = 0.5.

questions.q: A coin is tossed twice. How many outcomes are there in the sample space?
questions.e: S = {HH, HT, TH, TT}.

questions.q: What is the probability of an impossible event?
questions.e: An impossible event has no favourable outcomes.

questions.q: A card is drawn from a well-shuffled pack of 52. What is the probability that it is an ace? Give three decimal places.
Two dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum is 7? Give three decimal places.
questions.e: Six of the 36 outcomes give 7: 6/36 = 1/6 ≈ 0.167.

questions.q: If P(A) = 0.4, find P(not A).
P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.3 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.1. Find P(A ∪ B).
Three coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting at least one head? Give three decimal places.
questions.e: P(no head) = 1/8, so P(at least one head) = 7/8 = 0.875.

questions.q: A bag has 5 red and 3 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both are red? Give three decimal places.
A and B are mutually exclusive, with P(A) = 0.35 and P(B) = 0.45. Find P(neither A nor B).
Find the principal value of sin⁻¹(1/2), in degrees.
questions.e: sin 30° = 1/2, and 30° is in the principal range [−90°, 90°].

questions.q: Find the principal value of cos⁻¹(0), in degrees.
questions.e: cos 90° = 0, and 90° is in the principal range [0°, 180°].

questions.q: Find the principal value of tan⁻¹(1), in degrees.
Find the principal value of cos⁻¹(−1/2), in degrees.
Find the principal value of sin⁻¹(−√3/2), in degrees.
Find sin⁻¹(1) + cos⁻¹(1), in degrees.
questions.e: sin⁻¹(1) = 90° and cos⁻¹(1) = 0°.

questions.q: Find sin⁻¹(sin 120°), in degrees.
questions.e: sin 120° = sin 60°, and 60° is the angle in [−90°, 90°] with this sine.

questions.q: Find tan⁻¹(√3) − sec⁻¹(−2), in degrees.
questions.e: tan⁻¹(√3) = 60° and sec⁻¹(−2) = cos⁻¹(−1/2) = 120°, so the answer is −60°.

questions.q: For |x| ≥ 1, find cos(sec⁻¹ x + cosec⁻¹ x).
questions.e: sec⁻¹ x + cosec⁻¹ x = π/2, and cos(π/2) = 0.

questions.q: Find tan⁻¹(1/2) + tan⁻¹(1/3), in degrees.
questions.e: tan⁻¹ a + tan⁻¹ b = tan⁻¹[(a + b)/(1 − ab)] = tan⁻¹[(5/6)/(5/6)] = tan⁻¹ 1 = 45°.

questions.q: How many elements does a matrix with 2 rows and 3 columns have?
questions.e: A 2 × 3 matrix has 2 × 3 = 6 elements.

questions.q: A matrix with the same number of rows and columns is called a ______ matrix.
questions.e: For example, a 3 × 3 matrix is a square matrix of order 3.

questions.q: A is a 3 × 2 matrix. How many rows does its transpose have?
questions.e: The transpose of an m × n matrix is n × m, so Aᵀ is 2 × 3.

questions.q: A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]]. Find the sum of all the elements of 2A.
questions.e: 2A = [[2, 4], [6, 8]], whose elements add to 20.

questions.q: A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] and B = [[0, 1], [1, 0]]. Find the element in row 1, column 1 of AB.
questions.e: Row 1 of A times column 1 of B: 1 × 0 + 2 × 1 = 2.

questions.q: A square matrix A with Aᵀ = −A is called ______.
questions.e: If Aᵀ = A the matrix is symmetric; if Aᵀ = −A it is skew symmetric.

questions.q: How many 2 × 2 matrices can be formed if each entry is either 0 or 1?
questions.e: Each of the 4 entries has 2 choices: 2⁴ = 16.

questions.q: A = [[2, 0], [0, 3]]. Find the element in row 2, column 2 of A².
questions.e: The square of a diagonal matrix is found by squaring its diagonal entries: A² = [[4, 0], [0, 9]].

questions.q: A = [[3, 1], [−1, 2]] satisfies A² − 5A + kI = O. Find k.
What is the value of every diagonal element of a skew symmetric matrix?
questions.e: aii = −aii, so 2aii = 0 and aii = 0.

questions.q: Find the determinant of [[2, 3], [1, 4]].
If two rows of a determinant are identical, what is its value?
questions.e: Swapping the two equal rows changes the sign but not the value, so Δ = −Δ and Δ = 0.

questions.q: Find the determinant of [[5, 0], [0, 5]].
Find x if the determinant of [[x, 2], [4, 8]] is 0.
Use determinants to find the area of the triangle with vertices (1, 0), (6, 0) and (4, 3).
A is a 3 × 3 matrix with |A| = 2. Find |3A|.
questions.e: |kA| = kⁿ|A| for an n × n matrix: 3³ × 2 = 54.

questions.q: Find the determinant of [[1, 2, 3], [0, 1, 4], [0, 0, 5]].
questions.e: For a triangular matrix the determinant is the product of the diagonal entries: 1 × 1 × 5 = 5.

questions.q: A is invertible and |A| = 4. Find |A⁻¹|.
A is a 3 × 3 matrix with |adj A| = 64. If |A| is positive, find |A|.
questions.e: For a 3 × 3 matrix |adj A| = |A|², so |A|² = 64 and |A| = 8.

questions.q: For what value of k does the system x + 2y = 3, 2x + ky = 5 fail to have a unique solution?
questions.e: There is no unique solution when the coefficient determinant is 0: k − 4 = 0, so k = 4.

questions.q: Find dy/dx for y = sin x at x = 0.
questions.e: dy/dx = cos x = 1 at x = 0.

questions.q: Find dy/dx for y = eˣ at x = 0.
questions.e: d/dx (eˣ) = eˣ, which is 1 at x = 0.

questions.q: Find dy/dx for y = log x (natural logarithm) at x = 2.
questions.e: d/dx (log x) = 1/x = 0.5 at x = 2.

questions.q: Find dy/dx for y = sin 2x at x = 0.
questions.e: By the chain rule dy/dx = 2 cos 2x = 2 at x = 0.

questions.q: Find dy/dx for y = (x² + 1)³ at x = 1.
f(x) = kx + 1 for x ≤ 2 and f(x) = 3x − 1 for x > 2. For what value of k is f continuous at x = 2?
questions.e: The two pieces must meet at x = 2: 2k + 1 = 5, so k = 2.

questions.q: Find dy/dx for y = xˣ at x = 1.
questions.e: log y = x log x, so (1/y) dy/dx = log x + 1 and dy/dx = xˣ(1 + log x) = 1 at x = 1.

questions.q: x = t² and y = t³. Find dy/dx at t = 2.
questions.e: dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) = 3t²/2t = 3t/2 = 3 at t = 2.

questions.q: y = e^(2x). Find d²y/dx² at x = 0.
questions.e: dy/dx = 2e^(2x) and d²y/dx² = 4e^(2x) = 4 at x = 0.

questions.q: By Rolle's theorem, f(x) = x² − 4x + 3 on [1, 3] has a point c with f′(c) = 0. Find c.
questions.e: f(1) = f(3) = 0, and f′(x) = 2x − 4 = 0 gives c = 2, which lies in (1, 3).

questions.q: Find the slope of the tangent to y = x² at x = 3.
questions.e: dy/dx = 2x = 6 at x = 3.

questions.q: The radius of a circle increases at 2 cm/s. How fast is its circumference increasing? (π = 3.14)
questions.e: C = 2πr, so dC/dt = 2π dr/dt = 2 × 3.14 × 2 = 12.56 cm/s.

questions.q: What is the value of f′(x) at a local maximum of a differentiable function f?
questions.e: At a local maximum or minimum of a differentiable function, the tangent is horizontal: f′(x) = 0.

questions.q: Find the maximum value of f(x) = −x² + 4x + 1.
Find the minimum value of f(x) = x² − 6x + 10.
The side of a square increases at 3 cm/s. How fast is its area increasing when the side is 10 cm?
questions.e: A = x², so dA/dt = 2x dx/dt = 2 × 10 × 3 = 60 cm²/s.

questions.q: f(x) = x² − 4x + 6 is strictly increasing for x > a. Find a.
questions.e: f′(x) = 2x − 4 > 0 when x > 2.

questions.q: The volume of a cube increases at 9 cm³/s. How fast is its surface area increasing when the edge is 10 cm?
questions.e: dV/dt = 3a² da/dt gives da/dt = 9/300 = 0.03 cm/s. S = 6a², so dS/dt = 12a da/dt = 120 × 0.03 = 3.6 cm²/s.

questions.q: Two positive numbers add up to 16. What is the largest possible value of their product?
questions.e: P = x(16 − x); P′ = 16 − 2x = 0 at x = 8, so the largest product is 8 × 8 = 64.

questions.q: A wire 20 cm long is bent into a rectangle. What is the largest possible area of the rectangle?
questions.e: With sides x and 10 − x, A = x(10 − x) is greatest at x = 5: a square of area 25 cm².

questions.q: Evaluate the integral of 2x dx from x = 0 to x = 2.
questions.e: [x²] from 0 to 2 = 4.

questions.q: Evaluate the integral of 3x² dx from x = 0 to x = 1.
questions.e: [x³] from 0 to 1 = 1.

questions.q: Evaluate the integral of sin x dx from x = 0 to x = π.
Evaluate the integral of (1/x) dx from x = 1 to x = 2. Give three decimal places.
questions.e: [log x] from 1 to 2 = log 2 ≈ 0.693.

questions.q: Evaluate the integral of eˣ dx from x = 0 to x = 1. Give three decimal places.
Evaluate the integral of cos x dx from x = 0 to x = π/2.
questions.e: [sin x] from 0 to π/2 = 1.

questions.q: Evaluate the integral of x eˣ dx from x = 0 to x = 1.
questions.e: By parts, ∫x eˣ dx = x eˣ − eˣ. From 0 to 1: (e − e) − (0 − 1) = 1.

questions.q: Evaluate the integral of x³ dx from x = −1 to x = 1.
questions.e: x³ is an odd function, so its integral over a symmetric interval is 0.

questions.q: Evaluate the integral of sin² x dx from x = 0 to x = π/2. Give three decimal places.
questions.e: sin² x = (1 − cos 2x)/2, so the integral is [x/2 − sin 2x/4] from 0 to π/2 = π/4 ≈ 0.785.

questions.q: Evaluate the integral of |x − 1| dx from x = 0 to x = 3.
questions.e: From 0 to 1 the integrand is 1 − x (area 0.5); from 1 to 3 it is x − 1 (area 2). Total 2.5.

questions.q: Find the area under y = x between x = 0 and x = 4.
questions.e: Integral of x from 0 to 4 = [x²/2] = 8.

questions.q: Find the area under y = 3 between x = 1 and x = 5.
questions.e: It is a rectangle of width 4 and height 3.

questions.q: Find the area enclosed by the circle x² + y² = 1. (π = 3.14)
questions.e: Area = πr² = π × 1 = 3.14.

questions.q: Find the area under y = x² between x = 0 and x = 3.
questions.e: [x³/3] from 0 to 3 = 9.

questions.q: Find the area enclosed by the ellipse x²/9 + y²/4 = 1. (Area = πab, π = 3.14)
questions.e: a = 3 and b = 2, so the area is 3.14 × 6 = 18.84.

questions.q: Find the area bounded by y = x³, the x-axis and the lines x = 0 and x = 2.
questions.e: [x⁴/4] from 0 to 2 = 4.

questions.q: Find the area enclosed between y = x² and y = x. Give three decimal places.
questions.e: They meet at x = 0 and x = 1; area = integral of (x − x²) from 0 to 1 = 1/2 − 1/3 = 1/6 ≈ 0.167.

questions.q: Find the area enclosed by the parabola y² = 4x and the line x = 1. Give three decimal places.
questions.e: Area = 2 × integral of 2√x from 0 to 1 = 4 × 2/3 = 8/3 ≈ 2.667.

questions.q: Find the total area between y = sin x and the x-axis from x = 0 to x = 2π.
questions.e: Each half wave has area 2. The signed integral over 0 to 2π is 0, but area counts both halves: 2 + 2 = 4.

questions.q: Find the area of the region bounded by y = 2x, the x-axis and the line x = 3.
questions.e: Integral of 2x from 0 to 3 = [x²] = 9, the area of a triangle with base 3 and height 6.

questions.q: Find the magnitude of the vector 3i + 4j.
Find a · b for a = i + 2j + 3k and b = 2i + j + k.
What is the dot product of two perpendicular vectors?
Find the magnitude of 2i − 2j + k.
For what value of λ is i + 2j + λk perpendicular to 2i − j + 3k?
questions.e: The dot product must be 0: 2 − 2 + 3λ = 0, so λ = 0.

questions.q: |a| = 2, |b| = 5 and the angle between them is 30°. Find |a × b|.
Find the area of the parallelogram with adjacent sides a = i + 2j and b = 3i + j.
questions.e: a × b = (1 × 1 − 2 × 3)k = −5k, so the area is 5.

questions.q: Find the projection of a = 2i + 3j + 2k on b = i + 2j + k. Give two decimal places.
questions.e: Projection = a · b/|b| = 10/√6 ≈ 4.08.

questions.q: Find the angle between a = i + j and b = j + k, in degrees.
Find the area of the triangle with vertices A(1, 1, 1), B(1, 2, 3) and C(2, 3, 1). Give two decimal places.
questions.e: AB = j + 2k and AC = i + 2j; AB × AC = −4i + 2j − k, of magnitude √21. Area = √21/2 ≈ 2.29.

questions.q: Find the distance between the points (1, 2, 3) and (4, 6, 3).
If l, m and n are the direction cosines of a line, what is l² + m² + n²?
questions.e: Direction cosines always satisfy l² + m² + n² = 1.

questions.q: What angle does the x-axis make with the y-axis, in degrees?
questions.e: The coordinate axes are mutually perpendicular.

questions.q: A line has direction ratios 2, 3 and 6. Find its first direction cosine, l. Give three decimal places.
Find the angle, in degrees, between lines with direction ratios 1, 1, 0 and 0, 0, 1.
Find the distance of the point (2, 3, 6) from the origin.
Find the shortest distance between the parallel lines r = i + j + λ(2i − j + k) and r = 2i + j − k + μ(2i − j + k). Give two decimal places.
Find the angle, in degrees, between lines with direction ratios 1, 1, 0 and 1, 0, 1.
Find the shortest distance between the lines r = i + 2j + k + λ(i − j + k) and r = 2i − j − k + μ(2i + j + 2k). Give two decimal places.
Find the length of the line segment joining (1, 2, 3) and (4, 6, 15).
In a linear programming problem, the linear function to be maximised or minimised is called the ______ function.
questions.e: For example, Z = ax + by is the objective function; the inequalities are the constraints.

questions.q: The common region determined by all the constraints of a linear programming problem is called the ______ region.
questions.e: Every point in the feasible region satisfies all the constraints.

questions.q: Find the value of Z = 3x + 2y at the corner point (2, 1).
Maximise Z = x + y subject to x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 and x + y ≤ 5. What is the maximum value?
questions.e: Z = x + y can be at most 5 on the line x + y = 5.

questions.q: The corner points of a feasible region are (0, 0), (4, 0), (2, 3) and (0, 4). Find the maximum of Z = 2x + 3y.
questions.e: Z = 0, 8, 13 and 12 at the corner points; the maximum is 13 at (2, 3).

questions.q: The corner points of a feasible region are (0, 0), (4, 0), (2, 3) and (0, 4). Find the maximum of Z = 3x + y.
questions.e: Z = 0, 12, 9 and 4 at the corner points; the maximum is 12 at (4, 0).

questions.q: The corner points of a feasible region are (0, 2), (3, 0), (6, 0), (6, 8) and (0, 5). Find the minimum of Z = 4x + 6y.
questions.e: Z = 12, 12, 24, 72 and 30; the minimum, 12, occurs at (0, 2), (3, 0) and every point of the segment joining them.

questions.q: Maximise Z = 3x + 4y subject to x + y ≤ 4, x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0.
questions.e: The corner points are (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 4), giving Z = 0, 12 and 16.

questions.q: Minimise Z = −3x + 4y subject to x + 2y ≤ 8, 3x + 2y ≤ 12, x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0.
questions.e: The corner points are (0, 0), (4, 0), (2, 3) and (0, 4), giving Z = 0, −12, 6 and 16. The minimum is −12 at (4, 0).

questions.q: A dealer has ₹5760 to buy fans at ₹360 each and lamps at ₹240 each, and room for at most 20 items. He makes ₹22 on each fan and ₹18 on each lamp. What is his largest possible profit, in rupees?
questions.e: Constraints: 3x + 2y ≤ 48 and x + y ≤ 20. The corner points (0, 20), (8, 12) and (16, 0) give profits 360, 392 and 352, so 8 fans and 12 lamps give ₹392.

questions.q: A and B are independent, with P(A) = 0.6 and P(B) = 0.5. Find P(A ∩ B).
questions.e: For independent events P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B) = 0.3.

questions.q: P(B) = 0.5 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.2. Find P(A | B).
A die is thrown. What is the probability of a number greater than 4? Give three decimal places.
questions.e: Two outcomes (5 and 6) out of six: 1/3 ≈ 0.333.

questions.q: A fair coin is tossed 3 times. Find the probability of exactly 2 heads. Give three decimal places.
Find the mean of a binomial distribution with n = 10 and p = 0.3.
questions.e: Mean = np = 3.

questions.q: Find the variance of a binomial distribution with n = 10 and p = 0.3.
X takes the values 0, 1 and 2 with probabilities 0.3, 0.5 and 0.2. Find E(X).
Two cards are drawn one after the other without replacement from a pack of 52. Find the probability that both are kings. Give four decimal places.

Bag I has 3 red and 4 black balls; bag II has 5 red and 6 black balls. A bag is chosen at random and a ball drawn from it is red. Find the probability that it came from bag II. Give three decimal places.
A die is thrown 6 times. Getting an odd number is a success. Find the probability of at least 5 successes. Give four decimal places.
